text: In Java, why does a string holding one emoji report a length of 2?
choices: length() returns the number of bytes
The string contains an invisible joining character
Emoji are always stored as two separate characters
char is 16 bits, so characters above U+FFFF are stored as two surrogate values
explanation: Java's char was fixed at 16 bits when Unicode was expected to fit in 65,536 code points. It did not. length() counts 16-bit units, not characters, so codePointCount exists to give 1. It is a 1993 decision showing through, not a bug — and it is Chapter 1's fixed-width problem at a larger scale.
